summary: Reddit, X, Bluesky and most other platforms were blocked from this environment today, so this report rests on Hacker News threads only and has just 3 ideas that cleared the 2-independent-source bar. The strongest themes: people losing trust in domain registrars after the Namecheap seizure thread and the .name rug-pull, volunteer HOA boards with little accountability, and macOS system daemons that pin CPU with no good way to tame them.

ideas.title: Domain Safety Net
ideas.oneLiner: Watches your domains for registrar-side changes (lock status, nameservers, contacts, TLD policy changes) and keeps a ready-to-move backup of your DNS so a bad registrar day never takes you offline.
ideas.problem: Two HN threads in one week show owners being burned by registrars and registries: Namecheap reportedly seized and disabled one user's domains, support removed 2FA from an account after nothing more than "a good story and our username", and .name owners were hit by a policy change on third-level domains. Owners only find out after the damage, and have no exit plan or DNS copy ready.
ideas.targetUsers: Indie developers, small agencies and small businesses holding 3-100 domains, including many in India who use Namecheap, GoDaddy or Hostinger.
ideas.monetization: Free for 3 domains; Rs 199-499/month (or about $5/month) for unlimited domains, hourly checks and WhatsApp/Telegram alerts.
mvp: Add domains and poll RDAP/WHOIS for nameserver, transfer-lock (clientTransferProhibited), serverHold and registrar changes, with instant email/Telegram alerts
Expiry and auto-renew countdown with payment-method reminders
Daily DNS zone snapshot (A/MX/TXT/CNAME) exportable as a BIND file for one-click re-import elsewhere
Registrar risk checklist per domain: 2FA type, registrant email still reachable, recovery contact set
Exit kit page: step-by-step transfer-out guide per registrar with the EPP code request flow

competitors.name: Domain Locker (open source, self-hosted)
competitors.gap: Self-hosted portfolio tracker that watches DNS/WHOIS/SSL changes, but it needs hosting and setup, and it does not keep a restorable DNS backup or give an exit plan.

competitors.name: DomainDetails monitoring
competitors.gap: Documents what to monitor (nameservers, transfer lock, hold status) but is a guide, not a simple hosted product with backup and exit tooling.

ideas.title: HOA Board Ledger
ideas.oneLiner: A lightweight record-keeping tool for volunteer HOA and condo boards that logs votes, proxies, fines and appointments in a tamper-evident trail residents can read.
ideas.problem: In a 300-comment HN thread on Florida HOA foreclosures, residents describe boards that are accidental volunteers with no process, boards that self-appoint for 15+ years and use proxy votes to override objections, and boards that quietly sign deals with the builder's relatives. Owners can't verify what was decided or by whom, and volunteers don't know the rules they are supposed to follow.
ideas.targetUsers: Volunteer board members of small HOAs/condo associations (5-100 units) and the homeowners who want visibility into their decisions. US-first, but the same pattern exists in Indian housing societies and RWAs.
ideas.monetization: Per-association subscription of about $15-30/month, paid by the board; free read-only portal for residents.
mvp: Meeting module: agenda, minutes and per-motion vote record, with proxy and quorum counting
Append-only audit log of decisions, appointments and fines with timestamps
Resident portal showing minutes, votes, dues and fine history
Template governing rules (appointments, conflict-of-interest, fine caps and cure periods) with reminders when a step is skipped
Conflict-of-interest declaration on any contract or vendor vote

competitors.name: Board Beacon
competitors.gap: Aimed at volunteer boards with a transparency portal, but it is new and neither enforces the governing-rules process nor flags conflicts or self-dealing.

competitors.name: PayHOA
competitors.gap: Focused on dues and accounting for board burnout; weak on a resident-readable decision trail.

competitors.name: Loomio
competitors.gap: Strong on decision-making and voting, but not an HOA-specific records and compliance tool.

ideas.title: Mac Daemon Governor
ideas.oneLiner: A menu-bar app that spots macOS system daemons (mediaanalysisd, duetexpertd, WindowServer loops) pinning CPU, and applies per-process schedules, caps or safe restarts.
ideas.problem: Mac users report Apple's own background processes burning cores while idle, making laptops hot and loud. The existing throttler only helps partly ("it doesn't allow me to tame everything"), SIP blocks most manual fixes, and users resort to hand-curating lists of processes they distrust.
ideas.targetUsers: MacBook owners on Apple Silicon, especially developers and people running home-server Mac minis.
ideas.monetization: One-time $15-25 licence with a free tier that only monitors and alerts.
mvp: Live list of top CPU system daemons with plain-English explanation of what each does
Rules such as "if mediaanalysisd stays above 100% for 60s, restart it", using launchd kickstart where permitted
Quiet-hours and on-battery profiles that pause photo/media analysis
Crowd-sourced known-offender list with suggested rules per macOS version
Notification when WindowServer or menu-bar agents enter a runaway loop, with a one-click restart

competitors.name: App Tamer
competitors.gap: Throttles background apps and has an experimental kill-after-sustained-CPU rule, but its developer says throttling system daemons would disable what they do, so users still complain it can't tame everything.
